statement: You are given a grid of integers, matrix. A falling path starts at any cell in the top row and moves down one row at a time until it reaches the bottom row.
From cell (r, c) the next cell must be (r + 1, c − 1), (r + 1, c) or (r + 1, c + 1), staying inside the grid.
Return the smallest possible sum of the values along a falling path.

examples.explanation: Start at the 1, move straight down to the 5, then diagonally to the 7: 1 + 5 + 7 = 13.
Every path takes one 100 from the top row. Following it with the 1 below gives the minimum, 101.
